arxiv-1909-08355.title: Optimal Detection of Rotations about Unknown Axes by Coherent and Anticoherent States
arxiv-1909-08355.creator: John Martin, Stefan Weigert, Olivier Giraud
arxiv-1909-08355.description: Abstract Coherent and anticoherent states of spin systems up to spin j = 2 j=2 are known to be optimal in order to detect rotations by a known angle but unknown rotation axis. These optimal quantum rotosensors are characterized by minimal fidelity, given by the overlap of a state before and after a rotation, averaged over all directions in space.

arxiv-2008-01887.title: Finite-time blow-up prevention by logistic source in parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis models with singular sensitivity in any dimensional setting
arxiv-2008-01887.creator: Halil Ibrahim Kurt, Wenxian Shen
arxiv-2008-01887.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Halil Ibrahim Kurt, Wenxian Shen. In recent years, a lot of attention has been drawn to the question of whether logistic kinetics is sufficient to enforce the global existence of classical solutions or to prevent finite-time blow-up in various chemotaxis models. However, for several important chemotaxis models, only in the space two dimensional setting, it has been shown that logistic kinetics is sufficient to enforce the global existence of classical solutions (see [ 15 ] and [ 35 ] ).

arxiv-2107-04118.title: OCDE: Odds Conditional Density Estimator
arxiv-2107-04118.creator: Alex Akira Okuno, Felipe Maia Polo
arxiv-2107-04118.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alex Akira Okuno, Felipe Maia Polo. Conditional density estimation (CDE) models can be useful for many statistical applications, especially because the full conditional density is estimated instead of traditional regression point estimates, revealing more information about the uncertainty of the random variable of interest. In this paper, we propose a new methodology called Odds Conditional Density Estimator (OCDE) to estimate conditional densities in a supervised learning scheme.

arxiv-2107-12737.title: A Study of the Soft X-ray Emission Lines in NGC 4151 I. Kinematic Properties of the Plasma Wind
arxiv-2107-12737.creator: S. Grafton-Waters, M. Ahmed, S. Henson, F. Hinds-Williams, B Ivanova, E. Marshall, H. Udueni, D. Theodorakis, W. Dunn
arxiv-2107-12737.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by S. Grafton-Waters, M. Ahmed, S. Henson, F. Hinds-Williams, B Ivanova, E. Marshall, H. Udueni, D. Theodorakis, W. Dunn. We present our analysis of the narrow emission lines produced in the plasma regions within the bright active galactic nucleus of NGC 4151, from an ORBYTS research-with-schools public engagement project. Our goal was to test whether the properties of these plasma regions changed between XMM-Newton observations spanning 15 years from 2000 to 2015, by measuring the outflow velocities and distances.

arxiv-2404-19468.title: Compute-Forward Multiple Access for Gaussian Fast Fading Channels
arxiv-2404-19468.creator: Lanwei Zhang, Jamie Evans, and Jingge Zhu
arxiv-2404-19468.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lanwei Zhang, Jamie Evans, and Jingge Zhu. Compute-forward multiple access (CFMA) is a transmission strategy which allows the receiver in a multiple access channel (MAC) to first decode linear combinations of the transmitted signals and then solve for individual messages. Compared to existing MAC strategies such as joint decoding or successive interference cancellation (SIC), CFMA was shown to achieve the MAC capacity region for fixed channels under certain signal-to-noise (SNR) conditions without time-sharing using only single-user decoders.

arxiv-2405-01712.title: Multiplicity dependence of the p T p_{T} -spectra for charged particles and its relationship with partonic entropy
arxiv-2405-01712.creator: L.S. Moriggi 1, G.S. Ramos 2, M.V.T. Machado 2
arxiv-2405-01712.description: Abstract We investigate the multiplicity dependence of the transverse momentum p T p_{T} spectra of hadrons produced in high-energy collisions. We propose that the partonic distribution be parameterized by its non-extensive entropy and the parton saturation scale Q s ​ ( x ) Q_{s}(x) .

arxiv-2406-11291.title: Simulation of chiral motion of excitation within the ground-state manifolds of neutral atoms
arxiv-2406-11291.creator: Hao-Yuan Tang, Xiao-Xuan Li, Jia-Bin You, Xiao-Qiang Shao
arxiv-2406-11291.description: Abstract Laser-induced gauge fields in neutral atoms serve as a means of mimicking the effects of a magnetic field, providing researchers with a platform to explore behaviors analogous to those observed in condensed matter systems under real magnetic fields. Here, we propose a method to generate chiral motion in atomic excitations within the neutral atomic ground-state manifolds.

arxiv-2408-16414.title: Spectral Informed Neural Network: An Efficient and Low-Memory PINN
arxiv-2408-16414.creator: Tianchi Yu, Yiming Qi, Ivan Oseledets, Shiyi Chen
arxiv-2408-16414.description: Abstract With growing investigations into solving partial differential equations by physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), more accurate and efficient PINNs are required to meet the practical demands of scientific computing. One bottleneck of current PINNs is computing the high-order derivatives via automatic differentiation which often necessitates substantial computing resources.

arxiv-2508-06454.title: What Voting Rules Actually Do: A Data-Driven Analysis of Multi-Winner Voting
arxiv-2508-06454.creator: Joshua Caiata, Ben Armstrong, Kate Larson
arxiv-2508-06454.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joshua Caiata, Ben Armstrong, Kate Larson. Committee-selection problems arise in many contexts and applications, and there has been increasing interest within the social choice research community on identifying which properties are satisfied by different multi-winner voting rules (e.g. In this work, we propose a data-driven framework to evaluate how frequently voting rules violate axioms across diverse preference distributions in practice, shifting away from the binary perspective of axiom satisfaction given by worst-case analysis.

arxiv-2602-16348.title: Heat Equation driven by mixed local-nonlocal operators with non-regular space-dependent coefficients
arxiv-2602-16348.creator: Arshyn Altybay, Michael Ruzhansky
arxiv-2602-16348.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem for a heat equation governed by a mixed local–nonlocal diffusion operator with spatially irregular coefficients. We first establish classical well-posedness in an energy framework for bounded, measurable coefficients that satisfy uniform positivity, and we derive an a priori estimate ensuring uniqueness and continuous dependence on the initial data.

pmc-10572046.title: Aging, Inflammation, and Comorbidity in Cancers—A General In Silico Study Exemplified by Myeloproliferative Malignancies
pmc-10572046.creator: Johnny T Ottesen, Morten Andersen, Ognjen Arandjelović
pmc-10572046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryCancer escape links to the insufficient immune response. Thus, transition from a pre-cancerous state to cancerous development induced by morbidities competing for the immune resources is possible. We propose a simple but general conceptual model which suggests a unified explanation of cancer escape and other clinical and epidemiological observations, such as age-dependent prevalence and increased risk of getting cancer for patients with chronic inflammatory diseases.

pmc-10736329.description: Autism is characterized by patterns of neurological development that can cause differences in social interactions and sensory processing; restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior; and difficulties in identifying and describing feelings. pmc-13594863.title: Multi-omics and experimental validation identify RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
pmc-13594863.creator: Yanfei Chen, Xiaoxue Yu, Chao Cai, Jianming Lu, Xiaowen Lin, Zhimei Wen, Shu Li
pmc-13594863.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and multi-omics analyses reveal endothelial-enriched RAPGEF2 in KIRC.•RAPGEF2 independently predicts favorable survival across multicenter KIRC cohorts.•Experimental validation links RAPGEF2 to tumor suppression and immunotherapy benefit. Introduction

Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (KIRC) is the most common histological subtype of renal cell carcinoma (RCC), accounting for approximately 70%–80% of all RCC cases, and represents the major contributor to RCC-related mortality [1]. In recent years, the incidence of kidney cancer has continued to rise [2].
